concepts.title: Ecosystem: Structure and Function
concepts.definition: An ecosystem is a functional unit of nature where living organisms interact among themselves and with the surrounding physical environment.
concepts.key_idea: Biotic community plus the physical environment interacting as a system; varies from a pond to the entire biosphere.
question_patterns: define ecosystem and describe its structure
what are the components of an ecosystem
distinguish between terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems

concepts.title: Productivity in Ecosystems
concepts.definition: Productivity is the rate of biomass production per unit area over a time period, expressed as g/m²/yr or kcal/m²/yr.
concepts.formula: GPP = gross primary productivity; NPP = GPP - R
concepts.key_idea: Primary productivity depends on plant species, environmental factors, and photosynthetic capacity. NPP is available to consumers.
question_patterns: define gross primary productivity and net primary productivity
if GPP is 20000 kJ/m2/yr and respiration losses are 5000 kJ/m2/yr, find NPP
what factors affect primary productivity in an ecosystem

solution_steps.action: compute NPP from GPP and respiration
solution_steps.explain: NPP = GPP - R where R is respiration loss
net primary productivity is the stored biomass

concepts.title: Net Primary Productivity Calculation
concepts.definition: Net primary productivity equals gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (R).
concepts.key_idea: Only the net amount is available for consumption by heterotrophs.
question_patterns: if the gross primary productivity is 20000 and respiration losses are 5000, calculate NPP
a pond ecosystem has GPP of 15000 kcal/m2/yr and respiration of 5000, find NPP
calculate net primary productivity given GPP and R

solution_steps.explain: NPP is the energy stored as biomass

concepts.title: Decomposition Process
concepts.definition: Decomposition is the breakdown of complex organic matter into inorganic substances like CO2, water and nutrients by decomposers.
concepts.key_idea: Steps: fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification, mineralisation. Warm and moist environment favours decomposition.
question_patterns: describe the process of decomposition in an ecosystem
what are the steps of decomposition
how do temperature and moisture affect decomposition rate

solution_steps.explain: earthworms break down detritus into smaller particles
water-soluble inorganic nutrients percolate into soil
enzymes degrade detritus into simpler compounds
humus accumulates; microbes release inorganic nutrients

concepts.title: Energy Flow and 10 Percent Law
concepts.definition: Energy flow in an ecosystem is unidirectional. At each trophic level, only 10 percent of energy is transferred to the next level; the rest is lost as heat.
concepts.key_idea: Lindeman's 10 percent law governs energy transfer; energy decreases at successive trophic levels.
question_patterns: state Lindeman's ten percent law
if plants have 20000 kJ of energy, how much energy will reach the tertiary consumers
calculate the energy transferred to the second trophic level given the first trophic level energy

solution_steps.explain: only 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level

concepts.title: Energy Transfer Calculation
concepts.definition: Energy transferred to successive trophic levels is calculated by applying the 10 percent rule at each step.
concepts.key_idea: Each step loses 90 percent of energy as heat; only 10 percent is transferred.
question_patterns: plants capture 100000 kJ energy; calculate the energy available to tertiary consumers
if producers have 50000 joules of energy, how much reaches the secondary consumers
if the energy at the producer level is E, calculate the energy at the third trophic level

solution_steps.action: apply 10 percent law at each trophic step

concepts.title: Ecological Pyramids
concepts.definition: An ecological pyramid is a graphical representation of an ecological parameter (number, biomass or energy) at successive trophic levels.
concepts.key_idea: Pyramid of energy is always upright; pyramid of number and biomass may be inverted in some ecosystems.
question_patterns: what are ecological pyramids
which pyramid is always upright and why
give an example of an inverted pyramid of numbers

solution_steps.explain: pyramid of number, pyramid of biomass, pyramid of energy
pyramid of energy is always upright because energy is lost at each transfer
